coverage_gaps: Oil and gas remains under-mapped: LNG turbines, gas compression, pipeline integrity, produced-water treatment, drilling electrification, methane monitoring, gas-fired generation equipment, and pipeline permitting should be decomposed in a separate Layer 1B pass.

Renewables remain under-mapped beyond grid demand: inverter supply, grid-forming inverters, high-voltage cable, step-up transformers, storage balance-of-system, interconnection queues, and curtailment-management software require follow-up.
Utility regulatory economics, regional capacity markets, interconnection queue data, and load-growth evidence need primary-source validation before ranking generation owners or regulated utilities.
Market-cap buckets, liquidity, analyst coverage, short interest, ownership concentration, and valuation context were not fully verified in this merge layer.

Many candidate claims rely on provided search context or prior Layer 1B outputs; later layers should verify with 10-Ks, 10-Qs, investor presentations, earnings transcripts, DOE/NRC records, utility procurement documents, and regulatory filings.

The current universe is strongest in grid hardware, electrical infrastructure, and nuclear fuel-cycle nodes; it is weaker in oil/gas, LNG, renewables hardware, and energy software beyond utility grid-edge systems.

memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1 universe should rank companies by proximity to physical, regulated, or qualification-constrained bottlenecks created by AI/data-center load growth, electrification, grid expansion, and nuclear fuel security.
Transmission hardware remains one of the strongest underfollowed nodes because orders can precede visible EPC revenue and public pure-play exposure appears limited.
Transformers, switchgear, power-quality products, electrical distribution, conduit, and cable-management components form a schedule-critical layer for data-center and grid projects.
Nuclear fuel-cycle exposure must be separated into mining, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and fabrication because bottleneck severity and public-market purity differ materially by step.
Utility grid software, forecasting, power-quality monitoring, DERMS, and grid-edge visibility may become second-order chokepoints as utilities absorb large flexible and inflexible loads.

Oil and gas, LNG infrastructure, gas turbines, pipeline integrity, produced-water treatment, grid-forming inverters, high-voltage cable, storage balance-of-system, and renewables interconnection hardware need additional Layer 1B expansion.

Next layer must verify market cap, liquidity, valuation, sell-side coverage, backlog, revenue segmentation, customer concentration, and primary-source evidence for each candidate before raising or dropping priority.

summary: Merged Layer 1 Energy universe prioritizes chokepoint relevance across AI/data-center power demand, grid interconnection, transmission hardware, transformers/power-quality equipment, electrical construction, utility grid software, and nuclear fuel-cycle constraints. The universe intentionally balances reference leaders with underfollowed or second-order public-market mappings. Highest Serenity relevance is assigned to companies closest to physical, regulated, or qualification-constrained bottlenecks rather than broad energy exposure alone. This is a research-prioritization universe only, not a buy/sell list.
